messages:
jia: heads-up — noticed a slow rise in GPU pending count in us-central1-c for the last hour. small inference jobs (0.5 GPU) are placed everywhere except a group of nodes with 4 contiguous GPUs 

rafael: metrics? is this a taint/warmpool issue or a packing policy regression?

jia: looks like packing policy. scheduler is honoring nvlink-group affinity and topologySpread which are colliding with our 'minimize fragment' scorer. result: we end up scattering 0.5s onto many nodes instead of packing into a 4-slot node

claire: wait we set nvlink-group affinity for high-throughput sparse inference workloads to prefer certain node families. could that cause the scheduler to avoid nodes without nvlink locality even if they have free contiguous gpus?

rafael: yes — affinity is giving a strong positive weight to nodes labelled gpu.nvlink=group-a. but the fragment minimizer gives negative score when it would break other families' contiguous ranges. combined they create a local optimum that scatters.

infra-bot: [alert] scheduler_fragmentation: rising_unusable_slots us-central1-c. unusable_gpus=28 (4.6%), anomaly_score=0.64. eval_window=10m.

leo: what nodes are involved?

jia: quick inventory:
```
node-001 (gpu.nvlink=group-a): 4 free contiguous
node-002 (gpu.nvlink=group-b): 4 free contiguous
node-003 (gpu.nvlink=group-a): 2 free
node-004 (gpu.nvlink=group-b): 0 free
node-005 (gpu.nvlink=group-a): many 0.5s allocated across host
```

claire: node-005 sounds like the scatterer. what's the pod spec for those 0.5s? any affinity/anti-affinity set?

jia: spec excerpt:
```
resources:
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5
labels:
  workload-type: inference
annotations:
  redwood/scheduler-hint: prefer-nvlink=group-a
```

rafael: prefer-nvlink hint is sticky for these jobs. They were updated last week via rollout 2026-03-net-opt which bumped hint weight. I suspect the hint weight went from 0.2->0.9 in that rollout.

claire: ok. immediate mitigation: lower hint weight for prefer-nvlink to 0.4 and reduce contiguous-slot penalty for small fractional GPUs. Should allow better packing without losing locality for high-throughput cases.

leo: could we also temporarily run a targeted defragmenter that only moves 0.5-sized pods and packs them into group-a nodes that have full contiguous space? Lower risk than moving big jobs.

jia: i can run: `kubectl exec -n infra-tooling defrag --region us-central1-c --filter \"requests.gpu==0.5\" --target-label gpu.nvlink=group-a --dry-run`

rafael: also add a safety check: don't preempt pods with age <5m and don't evict more than 20% of small pods at once.

infra-bot: [note] defrag_job queued (id df-1142). initiated by jia.

jia: dry-run shows ~22 pods would be rescheduled and it would free 3 contiguous 4-GPU slots. expected win: schedule 3 x 4GPU backfills and reduce pending by ~14.

claire: good. schedule non-dry during low-traffic window in 10m. Also file a postmortem item to audit the 2026-03-net-opt rollout weight change. If the hint weight is too high, we should have a canary that tracks fragmentation metrics.

rafael: created INFRA-8822: \"nvlink-hint-weight-causes-scatter\" and assigned to eng-scheduler. includes suggested experiments (hint weight sweep, contiguous penalty tuning).

leo: follow-up ask: add cost metric to fragmentation alert — estimate token-hour lost or GPU-minutes stranded. we should correlate with billing to show customer impact.

infra-bot: [update] defrag_job df-1142 completed in dry-run; awaiting approval for execute.

jia: executing now with conservative thresholds. monitor events and OOMs.

(2m later)

jia: executed. defrag moved 18 small pods, freed 2 contiguous 4-GPU slots. two 4GPU training jobs scheduled and two pending batches drained. pending count dropped ~27%

rafael: thanks. put the weight rollback + small-pod packing heuristic in INFRA-8822 action items. we should also tweak the scheduler to prefer packing small fractional requests into nodes with identical nvlink label first before scattering.

claire: agreed. add unit tests for combined scoring of nvlink affinity + contiguous minimizer so future rollouts surface fragmentation diffs in precommit.

leo: nice recovery. closing unless we see new spikes. :white_check_mark:
